title: "It Would Make a Geordie Feel at Home": Regional Accent Perceptions and Speech Accommodation in Voice AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.38005v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems often perform less accurately for speakers of regional dialects, but less is known about how users respond to these limitations and how regional voices produced by voice assistants (VAs) are evaluated through a sociolinguistic lens. This study investigates these issues among speakers of Newcastle English (Geordies), examining both linguistic accommodation to voice technologies and perceptions of regional versus mainstream-accented VA voices. Participants interacted with a simulated VA that spoke either Newcastle English or Standard Southern British English (SSBE). They subsequently completed semi-structured interviews about their experiences with the experimental VA and voice technologies, language use, accent attitudes, and place orientation. The findings reveal a two-way process of sociolinguistic bias. The Geordie VA was associated with familiarity, warmth, personality, and local belonging,

translated_title: “这会让乔迪人（纽卡斯尔人）感到宾至如归”：语音AI中的地区口音感知与言语顺应
translated_abstract: 自动语音识别（ASR）系统在处理地区方言使用者时往往准确率较低，但关于用户如何应对这些局限，以及语音助手（VA）生成的地区口音如何从社会语言学视角被评价，目前所知甚少。本研究以纽卡斯尔英语（乔迪英语）使用者为对象，考察了人们对语音技术的语言顺应情况，以及对方言口音语音助手与主流口音语音助手的感知差异。参与者与一个模拟语音助手进行交互，该助手要么说纽卡斯尔英语，要么说英格兰南部标准英语（SSBE）。随后，参与者完成了半结构化访谈，内容涉及他们在实验语音助手及语音技术上的体验、语言使用情况、口音态度和地方认同。研究结果揭示了一种双向的社会语言学偏见过程：乔迪口音的语音助手让人联想到熟悉感、温暖、个性以及地方归属感。
tldr: 本研究通过与说纽卡斯尔方言或标准英音的语音助手交互发现，方言口音的语音助手能唤起用户的温暖感与地方归属感，但同时揭示了语音AI中存在双向的社会语言学偏见。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a two-way process of sociolinguistic bias in voice AI, showing that while a Newcastle (Geordie)-accented voice assistant evokes familiarity, warmth, and local belonging, regional accents are evaluated and accommodated differently from mainstream-accented voices.
